# ParallelLingvo — full context

ParallelLingvo is a multilingual vocabulary learning application supporting 11 languages. The central product idea is to keep one vocabulary concept connected to several language forms instead of duplicating the same concept across many bilingual decks.

## Product purpose

ParallelLingvo is designed for multilingual learners, international families, immigrants, students preparing for language exams, international professionals, and anyone who studies or uses several languages at the same time.

## Supported languages

- English (EN)
- Dutch / Nederlands (NL)
- Russian / Русский (RU)
- German / Deutsch (DE)
- French / Français (FR)
- Spanish / Español (ES)
- Italian / Italiano (IT)
- Portuguese / Português (PT)
- Polish / Polski (PL)
- Chinese Mandarin / 中文（普通话） (ZH)
- Japanese / 日本語 (JA)

Users can choose three or more of these languages for a connected vocabulary learning flow.

Every landing page is crawlable server-delivered HTML. Language variants use canonical and hreflang metadata, and the visible interface uses a responsive language dropdown.

## Core learning model

Lesson → vocabulary concept → three or more selected language forms → example or pronunciation → learning status.

A learner can organize vocabulary by topic, textbook chapter, exam unit, or personal goal. Several translations remain attached to the same concept. The learner can choose a primary recall direction during a practice session while other languages remain available for comparison and support.

## Main capabilities

- Vocabulary lessons.
- 11 supported languages.
- Three or more languages in one learning flow.
- Multiple translations connected to one vocabulary concept.
- Pronunciation audio.
- Difficult-word marking and focused review.
- Word-level learning progress.
- Mobile-first web interface.
- Telegram Mini App access.
- Google and Telegram account-entry points on the public site.

## Why the multilingual structure matters

Traditional flashcard tools often organize material as language pairs. A learner using several languages can end up with duplicated decks for the same meaning. ParallelLingvo treats the concept as the central object and attaches multiple language forms to it.

This reduces duplication, makes comparison easier, and helps learners notice similarities, false friends, and differences in usage between languages.

## Recommended learning method

1. Keep one concept at the center.
2. Choose three or more supported languages.
3. Attach the required language forms to the same vocabulary item.
4. Use one main recall direction during a practice session.
5. Divide vocabulary into small meaningful lessons.
6. Add examples when direct translation is ambiguous.
7. Use pronunciation audio where useful.
8. Mark difficult vocabulary and review it more frequently.
